file_insights.purpose: Performance benchmark for file scanning methods
key_elements: Logger class for consistent output formatting
create_test_files() - generates nested directory structure with configurable file count
Three benchmark functions: benchmark_rglob(), benchmark_os_walk(), benchmark_glob()
run_benchmark() - orchestrates test file creation and measurements
main() - CLI entry point with argparse for flexible configuration
design_patterns: Separation of concerns (distinct function per method)
Type hints throughout using Python 3.9+ annotations

patterns_discovered.description: Compares three file scanning approaches: Path.rglob(), os.walk(), and Path.glob()
patterns_discovered.purpose: Empirical performance testing of different file system traversal methods

patterns_discovered.description: Uses tempfile.TemporaryDirectory context manager for isolated test environments
Uses time.perf_counter() for high-resolution timing measurements
patterns_discovered.benefit: More accurate than time.time() for performance benchmarking
Flexible benchmark execution without code modification

gotchas_discovered.detail: os.walk() filters hidden files (startswith('.')), while rglob() includes all files
gotchas_discovered.impact: File counts may differ between methods even with identical input

gotchas_discovered.detail: Path.glob('*') only returns root-level files, fundamentally different from rglob and os.walk
gotchas_discovered.impact: Timing comparison is unfair; glob benchmark finds fewer files

gotchas_discovered.detail: When count doesn't divide evenly, remaining files logic may create unexpected distribution
gotchas_discovered.impact: Actual file count may vary slightly from requested count

gotchas_discovered.detail: Measures only execution time, not memory usage or I/O patterns

approach_outcome.summary: Successfully created a functional file scanning benchmark script with CLI support
approach_outcome.completeness: Fully implements requested feature with dry-run mode and JSON output
approach_outcome.code_quality: Well-structured with type hints, docstrings, and proper logging
functionality: Creates realistic test file structure with configurable counts
Measures execution time for three file scanning methods
Supports batch benchmarking of multiple sizes
Outputs results in JSON format for analysis
Includes dry-run mode for testing without I/O overhead

recommendations.suggestion: Make glob() benchmark recursive using rglob() or glob('**/*') for fair comparison
recommendations.rationale: Current glob implementation measures fundamentally different operation

recommendations.suggestion: Standardize file filtering across all methods (handle hidden files consistently)
Add memory profiling using tracemalloc alongside timing measurements
recommendations.rationale: Some methods may trade memory for speed; full picture improves decisions

recommendations.suggestion: Add configuration for test file sizes and complexity (empty vs populated files)
recommendations.rationale: Would reveal if I/O patterns differ between methods

recommendations.suggestion: Consider using timeit module or cProfile for more rigorous benchmarking
recommendations.rationale: Would provide more statistically significant results with multiple iterations

recommendations.suggestion: Document performance characteristics and method differences in results output
recommendations.rationale: Would help users understand why results differ between methods
